description: Builds the app and sends it to testers: iOS to TestFlight (signed with the certificate Ploa issues for this build), Android to Google Play internal testing (Ploa signs it with the upload key it keeps). By default it builds on this machine; where: "github" builds on GitHub instead, from the commit on the app's release branch (or sha), with the workflow Ploa wrote for the repo (the app's GitHub card in Ploa sets it up): Android on GitHub's Linux runners, iOS on the person's own Mac registered as a self-hosted runner with the label ploa (it waits for that runner), or on GitHub's Macs where an owner allowed them for the app on its GitHub card. GitHub counts these builds' minutes on the person's own GitHub account (free on a public repository; on a private one a Mac minute counts as ten of the plan's free monthly minutes, about 150 to 200 for an iOS build): say so before building iOS on GitHub's Macs. where: "cloud" builds on Ploa's own machines, from what's pushed to the app's linked GitHub repository, with nothing to set up and nothing counted on GitHub: each plan has a number of cloud builds a month; on Free each one waits a few minutes in a shared queue behind paid plans' builds, and stops at the month's count (say so, and that builds here or on GitHub never count); paid plans go first in line, and builds past the count add to the next bill (say so first). The answer says its place in the queue. where: "xcode-cloud" (iOS only) has Apple build and sign it in Xcode Cloud, from what's pushed to a branch (main unless branch names another), with the app's Xcode Cloud workflow; it needs that workflow made once in Xcode (ploa xcode-cloud in the app's folder says how) and counts against the person's Xcode Cloud hours with Apple. where: "gcp" (Android only) builds with Cloud Build in the workspace's own Google Cloud project, from what's pushed to the app's linked GitHub repository; an owner sets the project up once in Ploa's Settings › Builds (it says what to run in Cloud Shell), and Google bills its build-minutes to that project, never Ploa: the free tier's machine is free for 2,500 minutes a month but slow for Gradle (half an hour or more), and a bigger machine the workspace picked costs per minute from the first one (say which before building). Ploa still signs the bundle: no key goes to Google. On GitHub, in the cloud, in Xcode Cloud and in Google Cloud it builds what's committed and pushed, not local changes. where: "auto" builds on GitHub when that platform is ready there (ploa_github_status), else on this machine, and says which and why. It runs in the background, since a build takes minutes and Apple's processing up to half an hour, and returns a release ID right away; follow it with ploa_release_status. The build number is the next free one unless you pass one. Run ploa_preflight first. This never goes to App Review or production: those need ploa_release_submit_review or ploa_release_promote, and a person's approval.

applePlatform.description: With platform ios: the Apple platform to build, for an app whose target builds for several (a Mac, Apple TV or Vision Pro app). Default: the one the app's Xcode target builds for (iOS when it builds for iOS too). Mac, Apple TV and Vision Pro builds are made on this machine only (where here); a Mac app becomes an installer package, the app and the package each signed with Ploa's keys, which stay on Ploa.

branch.description: In Xcode Cloud: the branch to build. Default "main".

buildNumber.description: iOS build number or Android versionCode. Default "auto": one higher than anything the store has. On GitHub always "auto".

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

sha.description: On GitHub, in the cloud or in Google Cloud: the commit to build. Default: the head of the app's release branch.

where.description: Where to build: "here" (this machine, the default), "github" (from what is pushed; iOS on the person's self-hosted Mac runner, or GitHub's Macs if an owner allowed them), "cloud" (Ploa's machines, from what is pushed; counted against the plan's cloud builds), "xcode-cloud" (iOS in Apple's Xcode Cloud, from a pushed branch), "gcp" (Android in the workspace's own Google Cloud project with Cloud Build, from what is pushed; Google bills that project) or "auto" (GitHub when it's ready for this platform, else here).

workflow.description: In Xcode Cloud: the workflow's name, when the app has more than one.

title: Build and send to testers
